records.title: e-2008 Range Below Advertised
records.description: The electric e-2008 consistently delivers real-world range well below the WLTP figure, with owners reporting 30-40% reduction in cold weather. Battery management system calibration and heating energy draw are contributing factors.
records.solution: Perform a battery recalibration by fully charging then fully depleting the battery twice. Use eco mode and pre-condition while plugged in. A software update may improve BMS estimation accuracy.
symptoms: Rapid range drop in cold weather

citations.description: e-2008 real-world range reports and cold weather performance threads

records.title: PureTech 1.2 Wet Timing Belt Delamination
records.description: Peugeot confirms that previous-generation 1.0 and 1.2 PureTech engines can experience an oil-pressure issue resulting from premature timing-belt degradation. Official terms cover affected non-turbo engines produced June 2012-June 2022 and 1.2 turbo engines produced April 2014-June 2022. The 2008 uses a belt, not the timing chain incorrectly prescribed by the frozen solution; the shortened interval, revised-belt history and 130-owner count are not established by the cited manufacturer evidence.
records.solution: If an oil-pressure warning appears, stop the engine as soon as it is safe and do not continue driving until the lubrication system is checked. Identify engine and production date by VIN, inspect belt condition using the current Peugeot procedure, and when degradation is confirmed follow engine-specific instructions for the timing-belt system, oil pickup/lubrication circuit, oil and filter. Check Peugeot support eligibility and the service schedule. Do not buy a timing-belt kit from this page; production date, engine, diagnosis and VIN fitment must be established first.
symptoms: belt condition assessed under current procedure
oil pickup and lubrication consequences checked

records.title: 'Anti-Pollution Fault' Warning — Emissions System Faults
records.description: A very common 206 complaint on multiplexed cars is the 'Anti-pollution fault' message on the multifunction display, often accompanied by the engine management light, misfire, lost power or limp mode. It is a generic emissions-system alert triggered by a range of root causes documented across owner forums: failing ignition coils, lambda (oxygen) sensor faults, sticking EGR valves, sticky hydraulic tappets and, on neglected cars, catalytic converters damaged by sustained misfiring. Because the message is generic, owners frequently replace the wrong parts before reading the stored fault codes.
records.solution: Read the stored DTCs with PSA-capable diagnostics rather than guessing; the accepted fixes are replacing the specific failed component — most commonly an ignition coil pack or lambda sensor, cleaning or replacing the EGR valve, or replacing a misfire-damaged catalytic converter in advanced cases.
symptoms: 'Anti-pollution fault' message on the multifunction display
Misfire or juddering, especially under load
Loss of power or limp mode
Engine cutting out shortly after the warning appears

records.title: BSI (Built-in Systems Interface) Body Control Unit Faults
records.description: The 206's BSI body control computer, which governs central locking, wipers, lights, instrument functions and the immobiliser, is prone to corrupted software, dry solder joints and water ingress — water entering through the bonnet vent and poorly drained plenum chamber can drip onto the unit and fuse box. A glitched or failed BSI causes seemingly random electrical chaos: wipers and lights operating on their own, dead central locking, erratic dashboard readings, and immobiliser faults that leave the car unable to start. Owner clubs maintain a well-known battery-disconnect 'BSI reset' procedure because the fault is so widespread on multiplexed (mid-2001-on) cars.
records.solution: First attempt the documented BSI reset (controlled battery disconnect/reboot sequence); persistent faults require repair of the unit's solder joints by a specialist or a replacement BSI that must be coded/cloned to the car. Address water ingress at the bonnet vent and plenum drains to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: Car will not start with immobiliser/anti-theft fault shown
Central locking stops working or operates by itself
Wipers or headlights switch on without input
Erratic instrument cluster readings and warning lights
Electric windows and rear wiper dead simultaneously

records.title: COM2000 Indicator/Wiper Stalk Unit Failure
records.description: The COM2000 steering-column module — which combines the indicator and wiper stalks, horn contact and the multiplex electronics behind them — is a notorious 206 weak point, particularly on multiplexed cars built from July 2001. Worn or grease-fouled contacts cause indicators to self-trigger, cancel erratically or only work with the lights on, headlights to flash when indicating, and the horn to stop working. The fault was so widespread that Honest John records Peugeot offering a free fix in France from December 2002 and in the UK from January 2003 for cars under warranty.
records.solution: Replace the COM2000 unit (roughly £130-£180 for the part depending on trim, plus fitting behind the steering wheel); confident DIYers sometimes succeed in cleaning and re-greasing the internal contacts, but unit replacement is the accepted lasting fix.
symptoms: Indicators come on or cancel by themselves
Indicators only work with headlights switched on
Main beam flashes when using the indicator stalk

records.title: Fuel Gauge Sender Unit Failure
records.description: The in-tank fuel level sender on the 206 commonly fails or misreads: the float arm sticks at certain levels, the resistive track wears, or the connector terminals on top of the pump/sender module corrode and lose contact. Owners see the gauge stuck on full or empty, wild fluctuation between readings, or a permanently lit low-fuel light, making it easy to run out of fuel unexpectedly. The fault is well documented across 206 owner forums with established access and repair procedures.
records.solution: Access the sender through the hatch under the rear seat cushion, clean and re-tension the connector terminals and inspect the wiring; if the float or resistive track is worn, replace the sender (or combined pump/sender) unit. No tank removal is required.
symptoms: Fuel gauge stuck on full or empty
Low fuel warning light on with a full tank
Gauge reading changes after hitting bumps
Running out of fuel despite gauge showing remaining range

records.title: Head Gasket Failure
records.description: The TU-series engines in the 206 are prone to head gasket failure, particularly when the cooling system is neglected. Overheating episodes accelerate gasket deterioration, leading to coolant-oil mixing and white exhaust smoke.
records.solution: Replace the head gasket, machine the cylinder head surface if warped, and flush the cooling system. Inspect and replace the thermostat and water pump preventatively.

records.title: Ignition Coil Pack Failure (Petrol TU Engines)
records.description: The wasted-spark coil pack on the 206's small petrol engines (1.1 KFV, 1.4 KFW and related TU units) is a frequent failure item: one of the two internal coils breaks down, dropping spark on a paired set of cylinders (1/4 or 2/3). Owners report intermittent misfire, rough running, the engine cutting out and refusing to restart until it cools, and the management light flickering. Forum consensus also warns that cheap aftermarket replacement packs often fail repeatedly or seat poorly, causing the fault to return.
records.solution: Replace the coil pack — OEM-quality (Sagem/Valeo/Bosch) units are strongly recommended over cheap aftermarket packs — along with spark plugs if worn. The job is a straightforward DIY or sub-one-hour shop task on these engines.
symptoms: Misfire on two cylinders, rough idle
Intermittent stalling or cutting out, restarts after cooling
Engine management light flickering or on
Hesitation and loss of power under acceleration
Hard or failed starting in damp weather

records.title: Power Steering Pump Leak
records.description: The hydraulic power steering pump develops seal leaks over time, causing fluid loss and increasingly heavy steering. The pump housing seals harden with age and mileage exposure.
records.solution: Replace the power steering pump seals or the complete pump assembly. Flush and refill the power steering fluid system.

citations.description: 206 power steering pump leak and seal failure reports

records.title: Rear Axle Torsion Beam Trailing Arm Bearing Wear
records.description: The 206's rear torsion-beam axle uses needle roller bearings on the trailing arm shafts that are poorly sealed against the elements; water ingress rusts the bearings away, and the failed rollers then chew up the arm shaft and the inside of the axle tube. The result is the classic PSA rear-end failure: knocking over bumps, visible negative camber on the rear wheels, wheel wobble and rapid inner-edge tyre wear. Left unattended, severe play degrades handling and the axle tube itself is destroyed, making a simple bearing kit repair impossible.
records.solution: If caught early, fit a trailing arm bearing and shaft repair kit; once the axle tube bearing surfaces are scored, the accepted fix is a fully reconditioned exchange rear axle from a specialist, followed by rear geometry/ride-height check. Repairing a seized, rusted original axle DIY is generally considered impractical.
symptoms: Knocking, clicking or squeaking from the rear over bumps
Rear wheels leaning in at the top (negative camber)
Rear wheel wobble visible when following the car
Excessive play when rocking the rear wheel
Rapid wear on the inner edges of the rear tyres
Rear ride height lower on one side

records.title: Window Regulator Failure
records.description: The electric window regulators on the 206 are a well-known weak point, with the cable-driven mechanism snapping or the motor failing. Front windows are most commonly affected, often dropping into the door.
records.solution: Replace the window regulator assembly. Upgraded aftermarket units with reinforced cables are available and recommended over OEM replacements.

records.title: Gearbox Input Shaft Bearing Noise
records.description: The MA/BE-series manual gearbox develops a characteristic whining or rumbling noise from the input shaft bearing. The noise is present in neutral with the clutch engaged and disappears when the pedal is pressed.
records.solution: Replace the input shaft bearing. This requires gearbox removal but is significantly cheaper than a full gearbox replacement if caught early.

citations.description: 207 BE4 gearbox bearing noise diagnosis and repair threads

records.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure
records.description: The Prince-family EP6 engine suffers from premature timing chain tensioner failure, causing chain slack and potential valve-to-piston contact. Early production units had an undersized tensioner that was later revised.
records.solution: Replace the timing chain, tensioner, and guides with the updated revision parts. Ensure correct oil specification (0W-30) is used to maintain hydraulic tensioner pressure.

citations.description: 207 EP6 timing chain tensioner failures and revised part numbers

records.title: Turbocharger Oil Leak
records.description: The turbocharger oil feed and return lines develop leaks on the 1.6 THP engine, leading to oil consumption and blue exhaust smoke. The turbo bearing seals also deteriorate with extended oil change intervals.
records.solution: Replace the turbo oil feed and return lines with updated gaskets. If bearings are worn, a turbo rebuild or replacement is necessary. Use manufacturer-recommended oil change intervals.

citations.description: 207 GTi turbo oil leak and THP engine oil consumption threads

records.title: AdBlue/SCR System Failure on BlueHDi Diesels — Urea Fault With Start-Prevention Countdown
records.description: BlueHDi diesel 208s suffer chronic AdBlue (SCR) system failures: the urea injection pump and its control electronics are integrated into the AdBlue tank, and pump seizure, urea crystallisation, faulty level sensors and (on pre-2018 cars) a non-vented filler cap that pulls a vacuum in the tank all kill urea delivery. The ECU then logs faults such as P20E8 (reductant pressure too low) or P20EE, lights the UREA/engine warning and starts a countdown (typically 1,100 km) after which the engine is prevented from starting. Peugeot's official fix is a complete new AdBlue tank assembly with ECU coding, quoted around GBP 1,100-1,300 at UK dealers.
records.solution: Diagnose which SCR component failed — NOx sensors and the AdBlue injector should be checked first, but a dead in-tank pump means a replacement AdBlue tank assembly that must be coded and primed to the car. Independent specialists and aftermarket repair kits can substantially undercut dealer pricing; do not ignore the countdown, as the car will refuse to restart at zero.
symptoms: UREA or AdBlue warning light with 'Engine fault: Repair needed' message
Start-prevention countdown in km shown on the dash
AdBlue level reads empty or incorrect despite being filled
Engine refuses to start once the countdown reaches zero
Repeated NOx sensor or anti-pollution faults that return after replacement

records.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Blockage
records.description: Diesel 208 models suffer from premature DPF blockage, particularly in vehicles used predominantly for short urban journeys. The DPF cannot complete its regeneration cycle during short trips, leading to progressive soot buildup.
records.solution: Perform a forced DPF regeneration using diagnostic equipment. For severely blocked filters, professional DPF cleaning or replacement is required. Advise regular motorway driving to allow passive regeneration.

records.title: e-208 Battery Recalls — Fire Risk and Sudden Loss of Drive
records.description: The electric e-208 has been subject to several EU safety recalls for its battery systems. Cars built 15 January to 20 June 2020 were recalled (Peugeot code KQJ) because a manufacturing error in the 12V battery under the bonnet can short-circuit and cause a fire while charging or driving. Separately, faulty battery control-unit software on 2022-2023 cars (recall MV4, RAPEX alert 16/2025, 23,704 vehicles; plus a 21,349-vehicle KBA-listed campaign) can make 'Ready' mode unavailable and cut propulsion without warning while driving; an AC-compressor wiring fault (recall MF9, Oct 2019-Nov 2022 builds) could also shut down the powertrain.
records.solution: All fixes are free dealer recall work: battery replacement/inspection for the 2020 fire-risk campaign and software updates for the battery control unit and AC compressor logic. Owners should run their VIN through Peugeot's recall checker and confirm campaigns KQJ, MF9 and MV4 have been completed.
symptoms: Sudden loss of acceleration or drive power while moving
Powertrain shuts down with electrical fault warning
Burning smell or overheating around the under-bonnet 12V battery (fire-risk batch)
Recall letter or open campaign shown against the VIN

records.title: e-208 Onboard Charger (OBC) Failure — AC Charging Stops Working
records.description: The Mahle-manufactured 11 kW three-phase onboard charger (CAOBC1) fitted to e-208s built between 2019 and 2023 is prone to premature failure, often beginning around 10,000-12,000 miles. Failing units first charge erratically or drop from 11 kW three-phase to ~7 kW, then stop AC charging entirely, leaving only DC rapid charging usable. The replacement unit must be dealer-coded to the vehicle, and a new OBC costs roughly EUR 2,200-3,800 at a dealer.
records.solution: Stellantis extended the OBC warranty to 4 years (from April 2021) and replaces failed Mahle units with a more reliable VMAX charger; outside warranty, a dealer-fitted new OBC or a cheaper remanufactured unit (e.g. ACtronics) is the fix. Owners with intermittent charging should have the OBC checked before the failure becomes total.
symptoms: Car intermittently refuses to charge on AC wallbox or granny cable
Charging speed drops from 11 kW to about 7 kW on three-phase
'Charging impossible' or charge-fault message on dash
DC rapid charging still works while AC charging does not
Unpredictable charge sessions stopping after a few minutes

records.title: EAT6/EAT8 Automatic Gearbox Jerky Shifting and Low-Speed Hesitation
records.description: The Aisin-based EAT6 (late 208 I) and EAT8 (208 II) torque-converter automatics generate widespread owner complaints about jerky or harsh shifts at low speed, lag and flaring in 2nd gear, hesitation when accelerating from 2,000-3,000 rpm, and jerking on light-throttle deceleration in traffic. The behaviour stems from aggressive fuel-saving shift calibration and torque-management software, made worse by ageing transmission fluid; in a minority of cases valve-body or clutch-pack wear is involved. It is consistently reported across Peugeot Forums, the 208 Owners Club and UK gearbox specialists rather than being isolated complaints.
records.solution: A dealer TCU software update and adaptation reset resolves most low-speed jerkiness, and a transmission fluid service helps on higher-mileage cars even though Peugeot calls the box sealed-for-life. Persistent flaring or slipping needs a gearbox specialist to inspect the valve body and clutches.
symptoms: Jerky or harsh gear changes at low speed, especially 1st-3rd
Lag or flare when 2nd gear engages
Jerking when decelerating slowly in traffic
Shifts smoother once the gearbox is warm

records.title: Front Suspension Knocking — Drop Links, Anti-Roll Bar Bushes and Damper Knock
records.description: First-generation 208s commonly develop knocking, clunking or rattling from the front suspension over bumps and rough surfaces. The usual culprits are worn ball-joint-type anti-roll bar drop links and perished ARB bushes, but 'damper knock' from the front struts and worn top mounts is also a well-known trait of the shared 208/2008/308 (T9) front suspension, which is why some owners replace drop links and still hear the noise. The noise is mainly an annoyance, but badly worn links and bushes degrade handling and will eventually fail an MOT.
records.solution: Inspect and replace worn drop links and anti-roll bar bushes first — a cheap job at any independent garage. If the knock persists, check strut top mounts and the dampers themselves, as 208 damper knock often requires new front shock absorbers.
symptoms: Knocking or clunking from the front over bumps and potholes
Rattling from one side of the front suspension on rough roads
Creaking or squeaking when the body rolls or over speed bumps
Noise persists after drop links have been replaced (damper/top-mount knock)
Vague or rattly feel through the steering on broken surfaces

records.title: 1.2 PureTech Wet Timing Belt Degradation (Oil Contamination, Brake Assist Loss)
records.description: The 1.2 PureTech (EB2) three-cylinder petrol engine uses a timing belt that runs inside the engine oil ('wet belt'). The belt rubber degrades prematurely in aged or incorrect-spec oil, shedding particles that clog the oil pickup, oil ways and the brake vacuum pump, causing oil starvation, engine damage and loss of braking assistance. Stellantis launched UK safety recall R/2020/326 (campaign JZR) covering 22,580 vehicles including 3008 I and 3008 II built June 2013 to April 2017, and the wider belt problem on later builds has been handled through service actions and warranty extensions.
records.solution: Under recall/campaign JZR dealers update belt-wear detection software, inspect, and replace the timing belt and brake vacuum pump if contaminated; the sump and oil pickup should be cleaned of belt debris. Outside the recall, replace the wet belt early (around 6 years/60k miles rather than the original 10-year schedule) and use only the specified PSA B71 2010 0W-30 oil with shortened oil-change intervals.
symptoms: 'Engine fault: repair needed' warning on dash
Hard brake pedal / loss of brake assistance
Rough idle or misfires, loss of power
Black rubbery sludge visible under the oil filler cap

records.title: 1.6 THP/VTi (Prince EP6) Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Failure
records.description: First-generation 3008s with the PSA/BMW Prince 1.6 petrol engines (turbo THP 156 and naturally aspirated VTi 120) suffer premature timing chain stretch caused by a soft original chain and a tensioner that is starved of oil, aggravated by the engine's aggressive variable valve timing. A stretched chain rattles on cold start and can jump or break, putting the engine out of synchronization and risking valve-to-piston contact and full engine failure. Peugeot issued revised chain and tensioner parts and a TSB, and forum-documented failures occurred well under 60,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace the timing chain kit (chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets) with the latest revised parts as soon as cold-start rattle or cam/crank correlation codes appear. Frequent oil changes with the correct grade slow chain wear; some owners obtained goodwill or warranty repairs from Peugeot UK under the in-force TSB.

Engine management light with timing/synchronization fault
Rough running or loss of power
Engine cranks but won't start (chain jumped)

records.description: The second-generation 3008 BlueHDi models are plagued by AdBlue system faults, including false level readings and crystallized injectors. The vehicle displays a countdown to engine disable even with a full AdBlue tank.
records.solution: Replace the AdBlue quality sensor and injector nozzle. Flush the AdBlue lines to remove crystallization. Update SCR system software and reset counters.

records.title: BSI (Built-in Systems Interface) Module Faults Causing Erratic Electrics
records.description: The BSI module is the central body-electronics hub on the 3008 (BSI2010 on the Mk1, BSI EL3 on the Mk2), controlling the immobiliser, central locking, lighting, wipers and dash communication. Thermal cycling cracks its solder joints (particularly around the central-locking relay), and voltage instability from a weak battery or careless battery changes corrupts it, producing no-start conditions, immobiliser faults, hazard lights that won't cancel, bouncing door locks and random warning cascades. It is a long-documented Peugeot/Citroën weakness with an established independent repair industry around it.
records.solution: First perform the official BSI reboot/hard-reset procedure (controlled battery disconnect) and verify the battery and alternator are healthy, as voltage problems mimic BSI failure. Persistent faults are fixed by specialist BSI board repair (about $100–200) or a replacement unit coded to the car; many faults after battery changes clear with a dealer diagnostic reset.
symptoms: Car intermittently fails to start / immobiliser fault
Hazard or indicator lights flash and won't turn off
Central locking locks/unlocks by itself or 'bounces'
Multiple random fault messages on the dash at once

records.title: DPF Premature Blockage
records.description: The 3008 diesel variants experience premature DPF clogging, with the larger vehicle weight and urban usage patterns contributing to incomplete regeneration cycles. The issue is more pronounced in pre-2017 models with the older DPF design.
records.solution: Force a DPF regeneration via diagnostic tool, top up Eolys additive, and advise sustained motorway driving. Severe cases require professional DPF cleaning or replacement.

citations.description: 3008 DPF blockage reports and regeneration failure threads

records.title: EAT6 Automatic Gearbox Shudder
records.description: The Aisin-sourced EAT6 six-speed automatic transmission exhibits judder and hesitation during low-speed manoeuvres and when pulling away from rest. Torque converter lockup calibration and fluid degradation are primary causes.
records.solution: Perform a complete ATF drain and refill with the specified Aisin fluid. Update the TCM software to the latest calibration. Persistent cases may need torque converter replacement.

citations.description: 3008 EAT6 automatic shudder and torque converter judder reports

records.title: HYbrid4 Diesel-Hybrid System and Battery Faults
records.description: The 2012–2016 3008 HYbrid4 (2.0 HDi diesel + rear electric motor) suffers hybrid-system faults from two sources: ageing of the Ni-MH high-voltage traction pack under the rear seats, whose poor ventilation accelerates cell imbalance, and an undersized 12V auxiliary battery whose low voltage triggers cascades of spurious fault messages and no-start conditions. Owners report 'Hybrid System Fault' and reduced-power warnings, loss of electric drive (and with it the car's all-wheel-drive capability), and rising fuel consumption when the electric side stops contributing.
records.solution: Always test and replace the 12V battery first, since many phantom hybrid faults disappear with a healthy auxiliary battery (a trickle charger helps cars used for short trips). Genuine HV pack failures are addressed with refurbished or repaired battery packs from hybrid specialists at a fraction of the new-unit price.
symptoms: 'Hybrid System Fault' or reduced power warning on dash
Electric drive / EV mode no longer engages
Car fails to start or shows random multiple warnings

records.title: i-Cockpit Infotainment (NAC) Touchscreen Black Screen / Freezing
records.description: Second-generation 3008s with the i-Cockpit and NAC (Navigation Audio Connectée) head unit commonly suffer the central touchscreen going completely black, freezing, or rebooting in a loop every few minutes due to firmware bugs in the NAC software. Because climate control, reversing camera and parking-sensor displays run through the screen, owners lose access to those functions while it is down; the fault is the subject of Peugeot technical service bulletins.
records.solution: First attempt a soft reset by holding the phone/source button for around 10 seconds; the lasting fix is a dealer (or USB self-service via Peugeot Update) NAC firmware update per the TSB. Units that remain unresponsive after reflashing require replacement of the touchscreen or NAC module.
symptoms: Touchscreen goes completely black while driving
Screen frozen and unresponsive to touch
System reboots itself every few minutes
Loss of climate control adjustment, reversing camera and radio

records.title: Rear Self-Levelling Hydraulic Suspension Leaks (3008 I, 2.0 HDi/HYbrid4)
records.description: First-generation 3008s fitted with the rear self-levelling hydraulic suspension (mainly 2.0 HDi 150 and HYbrid4 versions) commonly lose fluid from the crimped flexible pipe connections at the centre of the rear axle, with failures reported at as little as 30,000 miles. Once the fluid leaks out, the rear suspension knocks and crashes over bumps and the self-levelling function is lost, and the OEM hydraulic unit is expensive and prone to failing again.
records.solution: The accepted fix in the owner community is to remove the hydraulic self-levelling unit entirely and convert to conventional rear shock absorbers (the dampers from the 1.6 model are a direct fit), a roughly half-hour job that saves several hundred pounds over replacing the hydraulic system. Repairing the OEM unit is possible but rarely worthwhile.
symptoms: Knocking/banging from the rear over bumps
Oil visibly leaking around the centre of the rear axle
Rear ride height sags, especially when loaded
Hydraulic fluid film on rear suspension pipes

records.title: 1.2 PureTech Wet Timing Belt Degradation and Oil Starvation
records.description: Peugeot confirms that previous-generation 1.0 and 1.2 PureTech engines can experience an oil-pressure issue resulting from premature timing-belt degradation. Its official terms cover affected 1.2 turbo engines produced from April 2014 through June 2022, matching the frozen 308 year identity only at the production-window level. The frozen brake-vacuum-line, recall-volume, catastrophic-failure and 2023 chain-conversion claims are not established by that source.
records.solution: If an oil-pressure or braking-assistance warning appears, stop as soon as it is safe and have the vehicle inspected before further driving. Identify the exact engine and production date by VIN, inspect the belt using the current Peugeot procedure, and when degradation is confirmed follow engine-specific instructions for the timing-belt system, oil pickup/lubrication circuit, oil and filter. Check Peugeot support eligibility and the service schedule. Do not buy a timing-belt kit, vacuum pump or engine from this page; diagnosis, production date and VIN fitment must be established first.
symptoms: timing belt inspected under current procedure
affectedSystems: oil-pressure and brake-vacuum assistance where applicable

records.title: 1.6 HDi (DV6) Turbocharger Failure from Oil Starvation and Sludge
records.description: The 1.6 HDi diesel in the 308 I is notorious for turbocharger failure caused by oil starvation: carbon sludge — aggravated by extended oil intervals, wrong oil spec and leaking injector seals — blocks the tiny gauze filter in the turbo oil-feed banjo bolt and the feed/return pipes, starving the turbo bearing. Documented cases show oil pressure at the turbo far below the 2.3 bar minimum, and a replacement turbo fails again quickly if the sludged feed pipes, sump and pickup are not cleaned at the same time.
records.solution: Replace the turbocharger together with new oil feed and return pipes and the banjo-bolt filter, drop and clean the sump and oil pickup, and flush the engine — about $1,200-2,600 all-in at an independent shop. Prevent recurrence with strictly shortened oil-change intervals using the correct low-SAPS oil and prompt attention to injector seal leaks.
symptoms: Whining or whistling noise from the turbo
Noticeable loss of power / limp mode
Engine management light with underboost fault

records.title: 1.6 THP Intake Valve Carbon Buildup (Direct Injection)
records.description: Because the turbocharged 1.6 THP (EP6DT/EP6CDT/EP6DTS) injects fuel directly into the cylinder, no fuel washes over the backs of the intake valves; oil vapour from the PCV system bakes onto the valves and ports as hard carbon. Deposits typically become symptomatic between 50,000 and 80,000 km, progressively restricting airflow and causing rough cold idle, cold-start misfires, poor throttle response and higher fuel consumption.
records.solution: Walnut-shell blasting of the intake ports and valves is the accepted fix (roughly $350-900 at independent specialists; dealer quotes can be far higher) and is worth repeating preventively every 50,000-60,000 km. Quality fuel and regular oil changes slow, but do not prevent, re-accumulation.

records.title: 1.6 THP/VTi (EP6 'Prince') Timing Chain Stretch and Cold-Start Rattle
records.description: The PSA/BMW co-developed 1.6 'Prince' engine (EP6 VTi and EP6DT/EP6CDT THP) in the 308 I and early 308 II suffers well-documented timing chain stretch, often before 100,000 km. The original chain was too narrow for the load and the hydraulic tensioner bleeds down overnight, producing the characteristic 'death rattle' on cold start; left unaddressed the chain can skip teeth, throwing valve timing out and risking severe valve/piston damage. PSA revised the chain, tensioner and guides (brown-to-white PVC guides) around 2012-2013, and extended oil-change intervals are a known aggravating factor.
records.solution: Replace the timing chain kit (chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets) with the latest revised parts as soon as rattle or cam/crank correlation faults appear — roughly $800-2,000 at an independent specialist. Shorten oil change intervals to about 6,000 miles/10,000 km with the correct low-SAPS 5W-30 to slow wear.
symptoms: Metallic rattle for a few seconds on cold start
Constant chain rattle at idle once stretch worsens
Engine management light with cam/crank correlation faults
Loss of power or limp mode

records.title: AdBlue System Fault
records.description: The AdBlue (SCR) system on BlueHDi engines triggers false fault warnings and countdown timers to engine disable. The NOx sensor and AdBlue injector are primary failure points, often caused by crystallized fluid.
records.solution: Replace the NOx sensor and clean the AdBlue injector. Flush the AdBlue tank if crystallization is present. Reset the SCR system counters with diagnostic equipment.

records.title: DPF Regeneration Failure
records.description: The 308 diesel models experience frequent DPF regeneration failures, especially in stop-start urban driving conditions. The additive-based DPF system requires periodic Eolys fluid refills that are often overlooked during servicing.
records.solution: Top up the Eolys DPF additive fluid, perform a forced regeneration, and clean the DPF pressure sensor pipes. Replace the DPF if soot loading exceeds recoverable levels.

citations.description: 308 DPF regeneration failure and Eolys additive system maintenance

records.title: EAT6 Automatic Gearbox Shudder and Jerky Low-Speed Shifting
records.description: The Aisin-built EAT6 six-speed automatic fitted to the 308 II has a widespread reputation for low-speed shudder and jerky shifts, particularly when cold, in crawling traffic, and immediately after stop/start restarts. Causes documented by UK gearbox specialists include degraded transmission fluid affecting torque converter lock-up, valve body spool deposits, worn clutch packs and outdated TCU software; ignored shudder accelerates torque converter and clutch wear.
records.solution: First steps are a transmission fluid and filter change with the correct Aisin specification fluid plus a dealer TCU software update, which resolves many cases for a few hundred dollars. Persistent shudder points to the torque converter or valve body, which cost roughly $1,500-3,500 to repair or replace at an independent gearbox specialist.
symptoms: Shudder or vibration pulling away at low speed
Jerky or harsh gearshifts when cold
Lurch or judder after a stop/start restart
Delayed engagement selecting Drive or Reverse
Gearbox warning light in advanced cases

records.title: EGR Valve Failure
records.description: The exhaust gas recirculation valve on diesel 308 models becomes clogged with carbon deposits, causing rough idle and poor performance. The electrically actuated valve sticks in the open or closed position.
records.solution: Clean or replace the EGR valve. Install an EGR cooler bypass blanking kit if permitted in your region. Update the ECU software to revised EGR control maps.

citations.description: 308 HDi EGR valve carbon buildup and cleaning procedures

records.title: Electric Parking Brake (EPB) Faults — Caliper Motor, Switch and Wiring
records.description: 308 II (T9) and later cars with the electric parking brake commonly throw a 'Parking brake fault' message with a flashing warning lamp, the brake refusing to release or failing to auto-apply. Documented root causes across owner forums include failure of the electric actuator motors on the rear calipers (water ingress/electrical failure), a worn EPB console switch, wiring harness faults, and a weak 12V battery; faults also frequently appear after rear pad changes if the actuators are not wound back and recalibrated with a diagnostic tool.
records.solution: Diagnose with a Peugeot-compatible scan tool first: a worn switch or weak battery is a cheap fix, while a failed caliper actuator motor requires a replacement motor or caliper followed by EPB recalibration. After any rear brake work, the actuators must be retracted and recalibrated electronically to avoid inducing the fault.
symptoms: 'Parking brake fault' message on instrument panel
Handbrake will not release or car feels held back
Parking brake fails to apply automatically
Fault appears intermittently or after rear pad replacement

records.title: DPF Blockage
records.description: The 5008 diesel shares the PSA DPF issues common across the range, with the heavier seven-seat body exacerbating regeneration difficulties. School-run and city driving patterns are the primary triggers for premature blockage.
records.solution: Force DPF regeneration, ensure Eolys additive is topped up, and incorporate regular extended motorway drives. Replace the DPF if ash loading is beyond cleaning capability.

citations.description: 5008 diesel DPF blockage and regeneration failure reports

records.title: Front Suspension Creak and Knock
records.description: The 5008 develops creaking and knocking noises from the front suspension, particularly over low-speed bumps and when turning. The anti-roll bar drop links and front strut top mounts are the primary culprits.
records.solution: Replace the anti-roll bar drop links and strut top mount bearings. Lubricate the spring seats if noise persists. Check for worn lower control arm bushings on higher-mileage vehicles.

citations.description: 5008 front suspension creak and drop link replacement guides

records.title: Diesel DPF Regeneration Issues
records.description: The 508 diesel suffers from DPF regeneration failures, particularly on first-generation models with the additive DPF system. Frequent short journeys prevent the regeneration cycle from completing, leading to progressive soot buildup.
records.solution: Perform forced DPF regeneration via diagnostic tool. Top up the Eolys additive system. For severely blocked units, professional off-car DPF cleaning is recommended before resorting to replacement.

citations.description: 508 diesel DPF blockage and Eolys system maintenance threads

records.title: DPF Blockage in Commercial Use
records.description: Partner and Rifter vans used for urban delivery work are extremely susceptible to DPF blockage due to the constant stop-start nature of commercial use. The duty cycle rarely allows for passive regeneration.
records.solution: Schedule regular forced DPF regenerations as part of fleet maintenance. Consider installing a DPF-friendly route into the daily schedule. Top up Eolys additive at each service.

citations.description: Partner/Rifter commercial DPF blockage and fleet maintenance advice

records.title: Sliding Door Mechanism Failure
records.description: The sliding side door mechanism on the Partner and Rifter develops stiffness and eventual failure due to roller and track wear. The door becomes difficult to open or close, and may jam in transit, particularly in colder weather.
records.solution: Clean and lubricate the door track and roller bearings. Replace worn rollers and the lower guide channel. Adjust the door catch striker plate alignment if the door does not latch correctly.

citations.description: Partner/Rifter sliding door roller and track wear reports

records.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure
records.description: The RCZ shares the EP6 timing chain tensioner weakness with other PSA/BMW Prince engine applications. The hydraulic tensioner loses pressure, allowing chain slack that causes timing skip and valve damage in severe cases.
records.solution: Replace the timing chain, tensioner, guides, and sprockets with the latest revision parts. Maintain strict oil change intervals with the correct 0W-30 specification oil.

citations.description: RCZ THP timing chain replacement guides and tensioner revision history

records.title: Turbocharger Oil Leak
records.description: The THP turbocharger develops oil leaks from the feed and return lines, and the turbo bearing seals degrade with heat cycling. Oil consumption increases progressively, and blue smoke appears under boost.
records.solution: Replace turbo oil feed/return lines and gaskets. Rebuild or replace the turbocharger if bearing play is detected. Ensure oil change intervals are not exceeded.

citations.description: RCZ THP turbo oil leak diagnosis and replacement threads
